newsitem.title: UK: Canadian bonds lead pack in mixed week -Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds lead pack in mixed week -Salomon.

text.p: Canadian bonds were the best performing government bonds during a mixed week for the markets, Salomon Brothers data showed on Friday.
The bank's world government bond index rose 0.06 in the week to October 17 in local currency terms, with only three countries posting positive returns.

Canadian bonds rose 1.09 percent on the week in local terms, after the Bank of Canada cuts its key bank rate to 3.75 percent on Wednesday. The move brought the bank's target range for the overnight lending rate down to 3.25-3.75 percent.
U.S. Treasuries took the silver medal, gaining 0.62 percent. The only other country to show a rise was the Netherlands, with a meagre return of 0.01 percent.

German Bunds lost 0.08 percent in local terms, while British gilts dropped 0.33 percent, hurt by a stronger-than-expected borrowing requirement figure and expectations that British base rates will not be able to fall any further.
Britain's public sector borrowing requirement totalled 3.41 billion stg in September, well above forecasts for a 2.7 billion stg shortfall.
French bonds lost 0.28 percent on the week in franc terms, after a public sector strike raised concerns among investors.
High-yielding bond markets clustered around the bottom of the heap, with Spain losing 0.85 percent, Sweden dropping 0.63 percent and Italy giving up 0.42 percent.
Convergence plays, based on hopes those countries would join European Economic and Monetary Union, were overdone and investors had lost interest, analysts said.
Japanese bonds lost 0.30 percent in yen terms.
In dollar terms, Canada was again the victor, pushing Britain and the U.S. into second and third place. Canada rose 0.98 percent, and Britain gained 0.96 percent.

There was no change among the worst performers, with Spain off 1.82 percent, Sweden down 1.57 percent and Italy down 1.54 percent. They were joined by Switzerland, which dropped 1.61 percent. Bunds lost 0.98 percent in dollar terms, and Japan slipped 1.09 percent.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
